s1.syndrome_frame: A chronic, gradually enlarging, itchy skin lesion with ulceration and bleeding on the mid-back
salient_findings: Gradual increase in size over 10 years
Occasional oozing of serosanguineous fluid and bleeding
Overlying ulceration and lichenification of adjoining skin
key_facts: The patient is a woman in her 60s
The lesion has been present since childhood
The lesion was initially pea-sized and asymptomatic
The lesion has gradually increased in size over the past 10 years
The lesion is itchy
There is occasional oozing of serosanguineous fluid and bleeding
The lesion is a well-defined erythematous plaque with overlying ulceration
The lesion is located on the mid-back, 1 cm left of the spine
Adjoining skin shows a horseshoe-shaped oval area of lichenification
Histopathological examination revealed a circumscribed tumor with apocrine epithelial lining
Tumor epithelium has multiple papillary projections with vascular, plasma cell-rich stroma
Immunohistochemical analysis showed p63 staining positive in myoepithelial cell layers

shortlist.label: Hidradenoma papilliferum
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological examination revealed a circumscribed tumor with apocrine epithelial lining and papillary projections, consistent with hidradenoma papilliferum

shortlist.label: Apocrine gland carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: The presence of atypical cells, mitotic figures, and areas of necrosis in the tumor epithelium suggests a malignant apocrine gland carcinoma

shortlist.label: Syringocystadenocarcinoma papilliferum
shortlist.why_kept: The tumor's papillary projections and vascular, plasma cell-rich stroma are similar to those found in syringocystadenocarcinoma papilliferum

shortlist.label: Cylindrocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: The tumor's circumscribed nature and apocrine epithelial lining are consistent with cylindrocarcinoma

shortlist.label: Apocrine adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: The presence of apocrine epithelial lining and papillary projections, along with atypical cells and mitotic figures, suggests an apocrine adenocarcinoma

raw.rationale: The histopathological examination revealed a circumscribed tumor with apocrine epithelial lining and multiple papillary projections, which is consistent with Hidradenoma papilliferum. The presence of p63 staining positive in myoepithelial cell layers also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Apocrine gland carcinoma
rejected.why: The lack of dermal invasion and the presence of a well-defined tumor with apocrine epithelial lining suggests a benign lesion, making Apocrine gland carcinoma less likely.

rejected.label: Syringocystadenocarcinoma papilliferum
rejected.why: This diagnosis is less likely due to the absence of syringomatous features and the presence of a well-defined tumor with apocrine epithelial lining.

rejected.label: Cylindrocarcinoma
rejected.why: The histopathological features do not match those of Cylindrocarcinoma, which typically shows a more aggressive and infiltrative growth pattern.

rejected.label: Apocrine adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: The lack of dermal invasion and the presence of a well-defined tumor with apocrine epithelial lining suggests a benign lesion, making Apocrine adenocarcinoma less likely.
